title: Double-Angle Computations in Quadrant II
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Suppose sin(theta) = 3/5 with theta in Quadrant II (pi/2 < theta < pi). Calculate the exact values of sin(2*theta) and cos(2*theta).

steps.title: Find cos(theta) via Pythagorean Identity
steps.explanation: Because theta is in Quadrant II, cosine is negative, so select the negative square root cos(theta) = -4/5.
steps.why: Pythagorean identity and negative horizontal coordinate in Quadrant II.

steps.title: Evaluate sin(2*theta)
steps.explanation: Substitute the sine and cosine values into the double-angle formula for sine.

steps.title: Evaluate cos(2*theta)
steps.explanation: Substitute into the double-angle cosine formula.
steps.why: Fundamental double-angle identity cos(2*theta) = cos^2(theta) - sin^2(theta).
